## 1. Purpose

This module closes the real-data modeling workflow by comparing GBLUP-ADE with
the four regularized ANN variants on exactly the same outer-assessment
individuals defined by the frozen real-data validation design.

Only previously saved model outputs are read here. No model is refitted, no
hyperparameter is selected, and no held-out prediction is modified.

Three principles define the comparison:

- every method contributes the same 75 `Trait x outer split` tasks;
- every task contains the same 39 held-out individuals for all methods;
- paired ANN-versus-GBLUP summaries are descriptive contrasts of repeated
  cross-validation results, not tests that treat the 25 folds per trait as
  statistically independent replicates.

Because BM, Cer, and Prod.Cor are on different scales, RMSE and MAE are compared
**within trait** and are not averaged across traits.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dir.create(
  "output/real/comparison/figures",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)
```

## 2. Inputs and frozen output contract

```{r packages-and-inputs}
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)

GBLUP_RESULTS_RDS <-
  "output/real/gblup/real_gblup_ade_results.rds"
GBLUP_PREDICTIONS_RDS <-
  "output/real/gblup/real_gblup_ade_predictions.rds"
ANN_RESULTS_RDS <-
  "output/real/ann/final/real_ann_results.rds"
ANN_PREDICTIONS_RDS <-
  "output/real/ann/final/real_ann_predictions.rds"

required_files <- c(
  GBLUP_RESULTS_RDS,
  GBLUP_PREDICTIONS_RDS,
  ANN_RESULTS_RDS,
  ANN_PREDICTIONS_RDS
)

stopifnot(all(file.exists(required_files)))

gr <- readRDS(GBLUP_RESULTS_RDS)
gp <- readRDS(GBLUP_PREDICTIONS_RDS)
ar <- readRDS(ANN_RESULTS_RDS)
ap <- readRDS(ANN_PREDICTIONS_RDS)

expected_ann_models <- c(
  "ANN_0",
  "ANN_L1",
  "ANN_L2",
  "ANN_L1_L2"
)

model_order <- c(
  "GBLUP_ADE",
  expected_ann_models
)

expected_traits <- c(
  "Prod.Cor",
  "Cer",
  "BM"
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(gr) == 75L,
  nrow(gp) == 2925L,
  nrow(ar) == 300L,
  nrow(ap) == 11700L,
  length(unique(gr$TaskID)) == 75L,
  length(unique(ar$TaskID)) == 75L,
  all(gr$Status == "ok"),
  all(ar$Status == "ok"),
  all(is.finite(gp$Predicted_Value)),
  all(is.finite(ap$Predicted_Value)),
  identical(
    sort(unique(gr$Trait)),
    sort(expected_traits)
  ),
  identical(
    sort(unique(ar$Trait)),
    sort(expected_traits)
  ),
  identical(
    sort(unique(ar$Model)),
    sort(expected_ann_models)
  )
)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Object = c(
    "GBLUP-ADE task results",
    "GBLUP-ADE held-out predictions",
    "ANN task-by-model results",
    "ANN held-out predictions"
  ),
  Rows = c(
    nrow(gr),
    nrow(gp),
    nrow(ar),
    nrow(ap)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Frozen model outputs entering the real-data comparison",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 3. Matched evaluation design

### 3.1 Task structure by model

```{r model-structure}
model_structure_rows <- vector(
  "list",
  length(model_order)
)

for (model_index in seq_along(model_order)) {
  model <- model_order[model_index]

  if (model == "GBLUP_ADE") {
    result_data <- gr
    prediction_data <- gp
  } else {
    result_data <- ar[
      ar$Model == model,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
    prediction_data <- ap[
      ap$Model == model,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  }

  predictions_per_task <- as.integer(
    table(prediction_data$TaskID)
  )

  model_structure_rows[[model_index]] <- data.frame(
    Model = model,
    Tasks = length(unique(result_data$TaskID)),
    Predictions = nrow(prediction_data),
    Min_predictions_per_task = min(predictions_per_task),
    Max_predictions_per_task = max(predictions_per_task),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

model_structure <- do.call(
  rbind,
  model_structure_rows
)

rownames(model_structure) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  all(model_structure$Tasks == 75L),
  model_structure$Predictions[
    model_structure$Model == "GBLUP_ADE"
  ] == 2925L,
  all(
    model_structure$Predictions[
      model_structure$Model != "GBLUP_ADE"
    ] == 2925L
  ),
  all(model_structure$Min_predictions_per_task == 39L),
  all(model_structure$Max_predictions_per_task == 39L)
)

model_structure |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Observed task and held-out prediction structure by model",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

### 3.2 Exact target and individual matching

Predictions are aligned by trait, repetition, outer fold, split identifier,
task identifier, and individual identifier.

```{r matched-targets}
comparison_keys <- c(
  "Trait",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID",
  "TaskID",
  "ID"
)

g_targets <- gp[
  , c(
    comparison_keys,
    "Family",
    "Observed_Phenotype"
  )
]

paired_targets <- merge(
  g_targets,
  ap[
    , c(
      comparison_keys,
      "Model",
      "Family",
      "Observed_Phenotype"
    )
  ],
  by = comparison_keys,
  suffixes = c("_GBLUP", "_ANN"),
  sort = FALSE
)

paired_targets$Phenotype_difference <- abs(
  paired_targets$Observed_Phenotype_GBLUP -
    paired_targets$Observed_Phenotype_ANN
)

paired_targets$Family_match <-
  paired_targets$Family_GBLUP ==
  paired_targets$Family_ANN

target_match <- aggregate(
  Phenotype_difference ~ Model,
  data = paired_targets,
  FUN = max
)

family_match <- aggregate(
  Family_match ~ Model,
  data = paired_targets,
  FUN = all
)

target_match <- merge(
  target_match,
  family_match,
  by = "Model",
  sort = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(paired_targets) == 11700L,
  all(target_match$Phenotype_difference < 1e-12),
  all(target_match$Family_match)
)

target_match |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 12,
    caption = "Exact held-out target and family matching relative to GBLUP-ADE",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Every comparison is therefore made on the same held-out phenotype for the same
individual in the same outer split.

## 4. Evaluation metrics

The terminal comparison uses the same task-level metrics already calculated by
R06 and R07.

- **Pearson correlation** measures linear association between held-out
  prediction and phenotype.
- **RMSE** and **MAE** measure prediction error on the original trait scale;
  smaller values are better.
- **Bias** is `mean(prediction - phenotype)`; values nearer zero are better.
- **Slope** is the prediction coefficient in `lm(phenotype ~ prediction)`;
  values nearer one indicate better proportional calibration, but slope becomes
  unstable when prediction variance is nearly zero.
- **R-squared** is `1 - SSE/SST`; it can be negative for held-out predictions.

```{r metric-definitions, include=FALSE}
metrics <- c(
  "Phenotype_Correlation",
  "Phenotype_RMSE",
  "Phenotype_MAE",
  "Phenotype_Bias",
  "Phenotype_Slope",
  "Phenotype_R2"
)

higher_better <- c(
  "Phenotype_Correlation",
  "Phenotype_R2"
)

lower_better <- c(
  "Phenotype_RMSE",
  "Phenotype_MAE"
)

zero_target <- "Phenotype_Bias"
one_target <- "Phenotype_Slope"
```

For paired contrasts, positive performance advantage always favors the ANN
variant. Higher-is-better metrics use `ANN - GBLUP`; lower-is-better metrics use
`GBLUP - ANN`; bias is compared by distance from zero; slope is compared by
distance from one.

## 5. Trait-specific model performance

```{r trait-performance}
analysis_cols <- c(
  "Trait",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID",
  "TaskID",
  "Model",
  metrics
)

all_results <- rbind(
  gr[, analysis_cols],
  ar[, analysis_cols]
)

trait_summary <- aggregate(
  all_results[, metrics],
  by = list(
    Trait = all_results$Trait,
    Model = all_results$Model
  ),
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

trait_summary$Trait <- factor(
  trait_summary$Trait,
  levels = expected_traits
)

trait_summary$Model <- factor(
  trait_summary$Model,
  levels = model_order
)

trait_summary <- trait_summary[
  order(
    trait_summary$Trait,
    trait_summary$Model
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

trait_summary$Trait <- as.character(
  trait_summary$Trait
)
trait_summary$Model <- as.character(
  trait_summary$Model
)

trait_display <- trait_summary[
  , c(
    "Trait",
    "Model",
    "Phenotype_Correlation",
    "Phenotype_RMSE",
    "Phenotype_MAE",
    "Phenotype_R2"
  )
]

trait_display |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Mean held-out performance by trait and model",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

### 5.1 Best model by trait

```{r trait-winners}
trait_winner_rows <- vector(
  "list",
  length(expected_traits)
)

for (trait_index in seq_along(expected_traits)) {
  trait <- expected_traits[trait_index]

  d <- trait_summary[
    trait_summary$Trait == trait,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  trait_winner_rows[[trait_index]] <- data.frame(
    Trait = trait,
    Best_correlation = d$Model[
      which.max(d$Phenotype_Correlation)
    ],
    Best_RMSE = d$Model[
      which.min(d$Phenotype_RMSE)
    ],
    Best_MAE = d$Model[
      which.min(d$Phenotype_MAE)
    ],
    Best_R2 = d$Model[
      which.max(d$Phenotype_R2)
    ],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

trait_winners <- do.call(
  rbind,
  trait_winner_rows
)

trait_winners |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Best mean held-out metric by trait",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

gblup_rmse_wins <- sum(
  trait_winners$Best_RMSE == "GBLUP_ADE"
)
gblup_r2_wins <- sum(
  trait_winners$Best_R2 == "GBLUP_ADE"
)
gblup_corr_wins <- sum(
  trait_winners$Best_correlation == "GBLUP_ADE"
)
```

GBLUP-ADE has the lowest mean RMSE in
**`r gblup_rmse_wins` of `r length(expected_traits)` traits**, the highest mean
held-out \(R^2\) in **`r gblup_r2_wins` of `r length(expected_traits)`**, and the
highest mean Pearson correlation in
**`r gblup_corr_wins` of `r length(expected_traits)`**. Metric-specific winners
are retained because near-zero correlations can coexist with small differences
in RMSE when models shrink strongly toward the trait mean.

## 7. Matched ANN versus GBLUP-ADE contrasts

Each ANN result is paired with the GBLUP-ADE result from the same trait,
repetition, fold, split, and outer task.

```{r matched-contrasts}
task_keys <- c(
  "Trait",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID",
  "TaskID"
)

g <- gr[
  , c(
    task_keys,
    metrics
  )
]

names(g)[-(1:length(task_keys))] <- paste0(
  names(g)[-(1:length(task_keys))],
  "_GBLUP"
)

paired_rows <- list()
paired_row_index <- 0L

for (model in expected_ann_models) {
  a <- ar[
    ar$Model == model,
    c(
      task_keys,
      metrics
    )
  ]

  matched <- merge(
    a,
    g,
    by = task_keys,
    all = FALSE,
    sort = FALSE
  )

  stopifnot(
    nrow(matched) == 75L
  )

  for (trait in expected_traits) {
    trait_data <- matched[
      matched$Trait == trait,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    stopifnot(
      nrow(trait_data) == 25L
    )

    for (metric in metrics) {
      ann_value <- trait_data[[metric]]
      gblup_value <- trait_data[[
        paste0(metric, "_GBLUP")
      ]]

      raw_difference <- ann_value - gblup_value

      if (metric %in% higher_better) {
        advantage <- ann_value - gblup_value
      } else if (metric %in% lower_better) {
        advantage <- gblup_value - ann_value
      } else if (metric %in% zero_target) {
        advantage <- abs(gblup_value) - abs(ann_value)
      } else {
        advantage <-
          abs(gblup_value - 1) -
          abs(ann_value - 1)
      }

      paired_row_index <- paired_row_index + 1L

      valid <- is.finite(ann_value) &
        is.finite(gblup_value) &
        is.finite(advantage)

      paired_rows[[paired_row_index]] <- data.frame(
        Trait = trait,
        Model = model,
        Metric = metric,
        N_total = length(raw_difference),
        N_valid = sum(valid),
        N_missing = sum(!valid),
        Mean_ANN = mean(ann_value, na.rm = TRUE),
        Mean_GBLUP = mean(gblup_value, na.rm = TRUE),
        Mean_raw_difference = mean(
          raw_difference,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Median_raw_difference = median(
          raw_difference,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Mean_performance_advantage = mean(
          advantage,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Median_performance_advantage = median(
          advantage,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        ANN_better = sum(
          advantage > 0,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Equal = sum(
          advantage == 0,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        GBLUP_better = sum(
          advantage < 0,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  }
}

paired <- do.call(
  rbind,
  paired_rows
)

rownames(paired) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  all(
    paired$N_total ==
      paired$N_valid +
      paired$N_missing
  ),
  all(
    paired$ANN_better +
      paired$Equal +
      paired$GBLUP_better ==
      paired$N_valid
  )
)

paired_primary <- paired[
  paired$Metric %in% c(
    "Phenotype_Correlation",
    "Phenotype_RMSE",
    "Phenotype_R2"
  ),
  c(
    "Trait",
    "Model",
    "Metric",
    "Mean_ANN",
    "Mean_GBLUP",
    "Mean_performance_advantage",
    "ANN_better",
    "Equal",
    "GBLUP_better"
  )
]

paired_primary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Matched ANN versus GBLUP-ADE contrasts; positive advantage favors ANN",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

`N_total` is the number of matched outer tasks, `N_valid` is the number with
finite values for both methods and the derived performance advantage, and
`N_missing` records undefined contrasts (for example, Pearson correlation when
a prediction vector has zero variance). The win/equal/loss counts therefore sum
to `N_valid`, not necessarily to `N_total`.

The counts describe how often one model performs better on the same held-out
outer task. They are not interpreted as independent binomial or t-test
replicates because repeated cross-validation folds share observations across
repetitions.

## 8. Held-out prediction dispersion

Prediction compression is evaluated inside each outer task for all five models.
This avoids conflating within-fold variance with between-model or between-fold
changes in prediction level.

```{r prediction-dispersion}
prediction_cols <- c(
  "Trait",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID",
  "TaskID",
  "Model",
  "ID",
  "Observed_Phenotype",
  "Predicted_Value"
)

all_predictions <- rbind(
  gp[, prediction_cols],
  ap[, prediction_cols]
)

dispersion_groups <- split(
  all_predictions,
  interaction(
    all_predictions$Trait,
    all_predictions$Model,
    all_predictions$TaskID,
    drop = TRUE
  )
)

dispersion_fold <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    dispersion_groups,
    function(d) {
      sd_pred <- sd(d$Predicted_Value)
      sd_obs <- sd(d$Observed_Phenotype)

      correlation <- if (
        is.finite(sd_pred) &&
        sd_pred > 0 &&
        is.finite(sd_obs) &&
        sd_obs > 0
      ) {
        suppressWarnings(
          cor(
            d$Observed_Phenotype,
            d$Predicted_Value
          )
        )
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }

      data.frame(
        Trait = d$Trait[1],
        Model = d$Model[1],
        TaskID = d$TaskID[1],
        SD_pred = sd_pred,
        SD_obs = sd_obs,
        SD_ratio = sd_pred / sd_obs,
        Correlation = correlation,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )
)

rownames(dispersion_fold) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(dispersion_fold) == 375L
)

dispersion_summary_groups <- split(
  dispersion_fold,
  interaction(
    dispersion_fold$Trait,
    dispersion_fold$Model,
    drop = TRUE
  )
)

dispersion_summary <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    dispersion_summary_groups,
    function(d) {
      data.frame(
        Trait = d$Trait[1],
        Model = d$Model[1],
        Median_SD_ratio = median(
          d$SD_ratio,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Q25_SD_ratio = unname(
          quantile(
            d$SD_ratio,
            0.25,
            na.rm = TRUE
          )
        ),
        Q75_SD_ratio = unname(
          quantile(
            d$SD_ratio,
            0.75,
            na.rm = TRUE
          )
        ),
        Min_SD_ratio = min(
          d$SD_ratio,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Max_SD_ratio = max(
          d$SD_ratio,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )
)

rownames(dispersion_summary) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(dispersion_summary) == 15L
)

low_variance_counts <- aggregate(
  I(SD_ratio < 0.10) ~ Trait + Model,
  data = dispersion_fold,
  FUN = sum
)

names(low_variance_counts)[3] <-
  "Folds_SD_ratio_below_0_10"

dispersion_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Within-fold prediction SD relative to observed phenotype SD",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

low_variance_counts |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Number of outer folds with prediction SD below 10% of observed SD",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Low dispersion is interpreted together with held-out correlation and error.
A model can obtain a modest RMSE by shrinking predictions toward the trait mean
while providing little discrimination among individuals.

## 9. Scientific interpretation

The comparison is deliberately metric-specific and trait-specific. RMSE and MAE
are not averaged across traits because BM, Cer, and Prod.Cor are measured on
different scales.

The primary interpretation uses three complementary criteria:

1. held-out Pearson correlation for individual discrimination;
2. RMSE/MAE for prediction error on the original trait scale;
3. held-out \(R^2\) and within-fold prediction dispersion for calibration and
   collapse diagnostics.

A model is not considered predictively useful solely because it reduces RMSE
through stronger shrinkage if its held-out correlation remains approximately
zero. Likewise, calibration slope is interpreted cautiously in folds with
near-zero prediction variance.

In the frozen real-data results, GBLUP-ADE has the lowest mean RMSE in
**`r gblup_rmse_wins` of `r length(expected_traits)` traits** and the highest
mean held-out \(R^2\) in **`r gblup_r2_wins` of
`r length(expected_traits)` traits**. It also has the highest mean Pearson
correlation in **`r gblup_corr_wins` of `r length(expected_traits)` traits**.
The remaining correlation winner is interpreted cautiously because the winning
mean correlation remains close to zero. Prediction-dispersion diagnostics show
strong shrinkage for both modeling families; L1-containing ANN variants show
especially frequent near-constant predictions, while GBLUP-ADE also exhibits
substantial within-fold variance compression. The real-data result therefore
supports lower held-out error for GBLUP-ADE without demonstrating strong
individual discrimination by any evaluated model.

These conclusions are specific to the frozen real dataset, marker QC,
family-stratified repeated nested cross-validation design, GBLUP-ADE
specification, and prespecified ANN search space. This module does not establish
a universal ranking between genomic mixed models and neural networks.

## 10. Output contract

```{r comparison-output-contract, include=FALSE}
WRITE_COMPARISON_OUTPUTS <- identical(
  Sys.getenv(
    "WRITE_COMPARISON_OUTPUTS",
    "0"
  ),
  "1"
)

COMPARISON_DIR <-
  "output/real/comparison"

MODEL_STRUCTURE_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_model_structure.csv"
)

TARGET_MATCH_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_model_target_match.csv"
)

TRAIT_SUMMARY_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_model_trait_summary.csv"
)

TRAIT_WINNERS_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_model_trait_winners.csv"
)

PAIRED_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_ann_vs_gblup_paired_summary.csv"
)

DISPERSION_FOLD_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_model_within_fold_dispersion.csv"
)

DISPERSION_SUMMARY_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_model_dispersion_summary.csv"
)

LOW_VARIANCE_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "real_model_low_variance_folds.csv"
)
```

```{r write-comparison-outputs, eval=WRITE_COMPARISON_OUTPUTS, include=FALSE}
dir.create(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  model_structure,
  MODEL_STRUCTURE_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  target_match,
  TARGET_MATCH_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  trait_summary,
  TRAIT_SUMMARY_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  trait_winners,
  TRAIT_WINNERS_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  paired,
  PAIRED_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  dispersion_fold,
  DISPERSION_FOLD_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  dispersion_summary,
  DISPERSION_SUMMARY_CSV,
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  low_variance_counts,
```
